assumptions: The count at struct+0x650 does not change between the gate's two reads; no intervening write to it exists in the gate or the wrapper.
The caller supplies at least count-1 records; a shorter array would read out of bounds natively and is rejected by the model.
Element pointers are non-null; a null element would fault natively and is rejected by the model.
The selector oracle returns a 32-bit result; the gate's usual 0/1 contract is the common case and the inversion is applied in full.

clean_path.status: all written Status bytes zero, message null

gate_semantics.count_source: signed 32-bit field at struct+0x650, where struct is the qword at source+0x40
record_fields: record+0x00 is the begin pointer of an 8-byte-element array
record+0x08 is the end pointer of that array

scan.scanned_records: first count-1 records; the last record is not scanned
scan.skipped: empty inner ranges and records past the last scanned index

gate_semantics.wrapper_args: source object, third argument, count minus 1 with 32-bit wrap
gate_semantics.wrapper_zero_result: report path with the bottommost-level message
gate_semantics.zero_field_found: report path with the upper-levels message

messages.role: upper-levels report, used when a scanned element field is zero
messages.text: Can't ingest_behind file as despite allow_ingest_behind=true there are files with 0 seqno in database at upper levels!

messages.role: bottommost-level report, used when the wrapper result is zero
messages.text: Can't ingest_behind file as it doesn't fit at the bottommost level!

not_claimed: Semantics of the selector's dispatch callee 0x5f6a820; the selector stays an oracle.
Status bytes 6-7, which neither the clean path nor the builder writes.
The contents of the second report slice (length 0 in both gate paths); only its length matters.
The containing function of the gate's own call site 0x5ec97ab beyond the site address.

status_builder.args: status object, code byte, byte1, byte2, first slice, second slice
status_builder.gate_use: code 4, byte1 0, byte2 0, second slice length 0
status_builder.header_writes: code byte at +0, byte1 at +1, byte2 at +2, zero word at +3, zero byte at +5, message pointer at +8
status_builder.message_rule: first slice, plus colon-space plus second slice only when the second slice is non-empty
status_builder.old_buffer: released when non-null; the new buffer is stored at +8
